meaning: The number 62 is best known from Daniel's prophecy of the 62 weeks that point to the Anointed One (Daniel 9:25–26).
description: The number 62 appears in the Bible primarily in Daniel 9:25–26, where the prophecy describes a time period of seven weeks plus sixty-two weeks from the decree to rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One comes. After the 62 weeks, the Anointed One shall be "cut off and have nothing," and the city and sanctuary shall be destroyed. The prophecy is one of the most debated chronological calculations in biblical literature, and both Jewish and Christian interpreters have attempted to link it to specific historical events. Beyond this prophecy, the number 62 has limited independent symbolic significance in the biblical tradition.

versions.meaning: The number 62 has limited direct symbolic meaning but is most famous for appearing in Daniel's prophecy concerning the 62 weeks (Daniel 9:26).
versions.description: In Daniel 9:25–26, 62 weeks (of years) are mentioned as part of the prophecy about the Anointed One (Messiah), stating that after 62 weeks an anointed one will be cut off. In Jewish tradition, this is often interpreted in connection with the rebuilding of the temple and historical events. The number can also be seen as a combination of 60 and 2, where 60 may relate to completeness and 2 to testimony or partnership, but this is not a prominent symbolic interpretation in traditional texts.

footnotes.text: In rabbinic tradition, the 62 weeks have been linked to the period from the rebuilding of the temple under Persian rule until the destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE. The Talmud (Sanhedrin 97b) discusses the ages of the world in connection with Daniel's weeks.

In Christian theology, the 62 weeks (plus the 7 weeks) are interpreted messianically, with the time calculation pointing to Jesus' public ministry and crucifixion. Many Christian commentators count the weeks as "year-weeks" (1 week = 7 years), resulting in a period of 483 years from the decree to rebuild Jerusalem.

Some interpreters have noted that the number 62 can be analyzed as a combination of 60 (which, in the sexagesimal numeral system, may relate to completeness) and 2 (testimony or duality), but this is not an established symbolic interpretation in traditional biblical texts.
